description:
Description of a carrier of a value. Also called property or characteristic.
The attribute is the valid single source of truth for values in the conceptual model.
According to first normal form (1NF) of the relational model an attribute value makes a statement about ONE aspect of ONE instance of the entity of which the attribute is a property. This means multivalued attributes and combined attributevalues are not allowed.

The flags 'repeated' 'historicised' and 'translated' indicate multivalue attributes for special purposes. This is no contratiction to 1NF as this indicators and its meaning allow a safe transformation into a 1NF model.

It is not necessary for this attribute to be managed in exactly this form in one of the systems.
The attribute definition is used as a reference for everybody who want to work with this information

AttributeId.description: typed ID unique over all attributes in this schema

SpecificAttribute.description: Description of properties for a Attribute only. To be combined with BaseAttribute

elementId.description: unique ID (over the whole model) of the Attribute for reference purposes

displaySeq.description: sequence number used to sort the attributes for display in an entity.

domainId.description: Reference to the domain, restricting the range of values for this attribute

descriptive.description: The attribute is an important property to understand the meaning of the entity. Key attributes are ususally descriptive.

historicised.description:
Must a history be kept for the values of this attribute over time?
This implies that in the software / datsbase a mechanism must be built to keep many timestamped values for a single attribute.

translated.description:
This attribute value is multilingual i.e. can exist in several languages. How many and what languages is to be decided on a project/application level.
Multilingual values of unique attributes must be unique in every language.
This falg implies that in the software / datsbase a mechanism must be built to keep many values (one for every language) for a single attribute.

BaseAttribute.description:
Description of a carrier of a value. Also called property or characteristic.
The attribute is the valid Single Source of Truth for values in the conceptual model.
According to first normal form (1NF) the relational model an attribute value makes a statement about ONE aspect of ONE instance of the entity for which the attribute is a property. This means multivalued attributes and combined attributevalues are not allowed.

The flags 'repeated' 'historicised' and 'translated' indicate multivalue attributes for special purposes. This is no contratiction to 1NF as this indicators and its meaning allow a safe transformation into a 1NF model.

It is not necessary for this attribute to be managed in exactly this form in one of the systems.
The attribute definition is used as a reference for everybody who want to work with this information

name.description: Conceptual name of the attribute, telling something about the role, meaning and use of the attribute. Must be unique (in every given language) among all attributes of this entity.

description.description: Purpose, usage, meaning of an attribute value hold by this attribute.

shortDescr.description: Short text to be displayed as help to understand the purpose of this attribute in user interfaces.

mandatory.description: Must this attribute always have a value?

repeated.description:
This attribute can have more than one value.
The sequence of the values is random and must not bear any semantic (otherwise the 1NF is violated)
This implies that in the software / datsbase a mechanism must be built to keep many values for a single attribute.

encrypted.description: The value for this attribute has to be encrypted in every storage environment

additionalProps.description: additional properties (aka user defined properties udp) are  any properties of an this element  added by the current modeller. They serve as an extension to the predfefined element properties.
